leads.title: Gender Equality Act B.E. 2558
leads.documents: Thailand's comprehensive anti-discrimination law covering sexual orientation and gender identity; bans discrimination against male, female or 'a person who has a sexual expression different from that person's original sex' with penalty up to 6 months prison and 20,000 baht fine, with exception for 'education, religion and the public interest'
leads.detail: Cited as Gender Equality Act B.E. 2558 (Thai: พระราชบัญญัติความเท่าเทียมระหว่างเพศ พ.ศ.๒๕๕๘) passed 13 March 2015, came into force 9 September 2015. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Marriage Equality Act - Amendment to Civil and Commercial Code
leads.documents: Legalization of same-sex marriage and joint adoption by married same-sex couples; replaces terms 'men and women' and 'husband and wife' with 'individuals' and 'spouses'
leads.detail: Cited as passed House 27 March 2024 and Senate 18 June 2024, endorsed by King Maha Vajiralongkorn, published in Royal Gazette 24 September 2024, effective 23 January 2025. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Constitutional Court ruling 2021 on Section 1448 Civil and Commercial Code
leads.documents: Ruled that Section 1448 interpreting marriages as only between women and men is constitutional; full ruling contained language describing LGBTQ people as unable to reproduce, against nature, different 'species' incapable of creating 'delicate bond'
leads.detail: Cited as 2021 Constitutional Court ruling on Section 1448. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Penal Code Amendment Act of 1997 (No. 14) B.E. 2540
leads.documents: Decriminalization context and equal age of consent; set age of consent at fifteen years regardless of gender or sexual orientation following 1956 decriminalization of private adult consensual non-commercial sodomy
leads.detail: Cited as Penal Code Amendment Act of 1997 (Thai: พระราชบัญญัติแก้ไขเพิ่มเติมประมวลกฎหมายอาญา-(ฉบับที่-14)-พ.ศ.-2540). No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Persons' Name Act
leads.documents: Legal avenue debated/passed 2007 allowing transgender people to change their names after sex change operation but not their legal gender; approval discretionary with individual administrators
leads.detail: Cited as 2007 National Assembly debate and Persons' Name Act creating name-change avenue but not legal gender change. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: UNDP 2019 survey on LGBTQ discrimination in Thailand
leads.documents: Documents verbal harassment (53%), sexual assault (16%), pretending to be straight (42%), family discrimination (47.5%), suicidal ideation (49%) and attempts (17%); trans women highest levels - 61% verbal abuse, 22% sexual assault, 11% physical abuse, 8% police harassment, 32% workplace discrimination
leads.detail: Cited as 2019 UNDP survey/report; also notes only 44% of LGBTQ respondents knew about Gender Equality Act vs 50% non-LGBTQ. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch 2021 report
leads.documents: Assesses implementation of Thailand's Gender Equality Act B.E. 2558 as spotty and inadequate
leads.detail: Cited as 2021 Human Rights Watch report on implementation of the law. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: International Labour Organization 2015 research
leads.documents: Documents substantial barriers to employment for transgender people including full-time work, executive positions, promotions; discrimination in job applications and 'daily discrimination and humiliation' cutting short careers
leads.detail: Cited as 2015 research for the International Labour Organization. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) 2014 report
leads.documents: Documents that LGBTQ people 'still face discrimination affecting their social rights and job opportunities' and 'face difficulty gaining acceptance for non-traditional sexuality' despite tourism promotion as gay-friendly country; also cited for barriers to education, bullying, lack of mandatory SOGI education
leads.detail: Cited as 2014 report by USAID and UNDP. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Bangkok Post op-ed 2016 by Paisarn Likhitpreechakul, Sogi Foundation board member
leads.documents: Documents corrective rape used to 'cure' lesbians, including case of father in Loei confessing to raping 14-year-old daughter for four years to stop her socialising with tomboys; warns practices normalised and murders categorised as crimes of passion because Thai legal system lacks hate crimes concept
leads.detail: Cited as 2016 Paisarn Likhitpreechakul op-ed in Bangkok Post. No URL visible in provided text.
